narrative.overview: The dashboard is set like a microcontroller datasheet: a white sheet, near-black ink, hairline rules, grey table header rows, and every block captioned as a numbered table or figure. It is a working remote, so the datasheet lends only type, palette, density and one signature move; the layout and controls are ordinary web controls. The signature move is the timing diagram: every saved IR button is drawn from its real mark/space durations, and while a send is pending a blue cursor sweeps across that diagram.
keyCharacteristics: White sheet, ink text, one action blue, red only for faults and the rule threshold.
Captioned tables and figures instead of cards.
Square corners, no shadows on surfaces.
Each IR code shown as its own timing diagram with a length budget (n / 600).

rules.name: The Blue-Means-Act Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue appears only on things that act or on the act in progress. Status text that is not an action is green, red or ink.

rules.name: The Bands-Are-Temperature Rule
rules.body: The cool-to-warm band colours paint temperature and nothing else.

rules.name: The Caption Rule
rules.body: Every table and figure is numbered and named in its heading or caption; no label ever sits above a heading.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the page floats except the chart tooltip.

dos: Do caption every module as a numbered Table or Figure.
Do show every command's round trip in the row and the Activity table: pending (blue), done (green), error or no reply (red), with the device's error explained in words.
Do keep numbers in tabular figures and units after values (30.0 °C, 59 %).
Do label demo or synthetic data on screen.
donts: Don't use cards, rounded tiles or shadows for modules.
Don't use Signal Blue for anything that is not an action.
Don't put a label or eyebrow above a heading.
Don't use the temperature band colours for anything but temperature.
